target_customer: Indonesian small shops and wholesalers who buy wholesale goods and keep books
problem: Small Indonesian retailers kept paper ledgers and bought stock through informal wholesale channels with little credit. CrediBook is a bookkeeping app plus a wholesale marketplace with buy now pay later.
business_model: Free bookkeeping app feeding a B2B wholesale marketplace with take rate and BNPL financing
product_category: SME bookkeeping and B2B wholesale marketplace

founders.name: Dekha Anggareska
founders.background_notes: YC page cites 8+ years of software engineering.

founders.name: Christian Lie
founders.background_notes: YC page: Head of Regional Manager at PAYFAZZ and 8+ years in the SME space.

competitors.name: BukuWarung
competitors.what: digital bookkeeping app for small B2C businesses

competitors.name: BukuKas
competitors.what: digital bookkeeping app for small businesses

competitors.name: Ula
competitors.what: wholesale e-commerce marketplace for small retailers
competitors.funding_then: raised 10.5 million dollars when five months old (TechCrunch, date not confirmed)

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile bookkeeping app plus marketplace, logistics and credit scoring needed solid but standard engineering and heavy operations.

defensibility.rationale: Bookkeeping data tied merchants to the app and informed credit, but ledger apps and marketplaces from funded rivals were close substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded rivals pursued the same wedge. A later source says Ula closed its business; CrediBook shows no acquisition or layoff report in searches.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2021 framed Indonesian wholesalers as heavily offline, with bookkeeping digitization as an entry point; the company reports 330,000+ businesses on its site, undated.

rebrands.why: Bisnis.com reported the rename; the spelling Joovan versus Jooalan differs between sources and the reason is not given.

brand_strength.rationale: Name explains the product (credit plus book) and runs a three brand family, but no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: CrediBook used bookkeeping to reach small Indonesian shops and then layered wholesale and pay later on top. It raised 1.5 million dollars in January 2021 and an 8.1 million dollar Series A in March 2022 led by Monk's Hill, and the company reports 330,000+ businesses on its site. Searches found no layoffs or sale, so the company looks like a surviving niche leader with strong funded rivals.
notes: Company site lists Alpha JWC as a backer, but a Jakarta Post report says it did not take part in the Series A, and CB Insights lists Insignia, so participation is mixed. DailySocial first called the 2021 round Series A and corrected it to Pre-Series A. YC page says founded 2020. Ula competitor page date not confirmed. Year of the CrediMart rename taken from the 2021-09 Bisnis article URL.
